coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Rock Block D1
record.summary: The residential half of Block D at 3rd and Mission Rock streets: a Residential Mixed Use tower entitled to 240 ft (one of three 240-ft sites with Blocks A and F) wrapping the Block D2 parking structure along Third Street, with roughly 250,000 gsf of housing in the EIR description. Unbuilt and still surface parking.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (see digitization_method): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines. The D1/D2 line is a land-use zone boundary inside one Design Controls block, not a lot line; the Appendix marks Block D's parcel dimensions as illustrative.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco / Mission Rock Partners, adopted April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m. D1/D2 split from Figure 1.1 (p.10) and the Block D standards sheet (Appendix p.190).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so joining status.csv to it would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential Mixed Use per the D4D's Land Use Plan. Max height 240 ft -- one of the three tallest towers planned for the site (tied with Blocks A and F), NOT a 'mid-rise' as sometimes described in secondary summaries. Sits at the 3rd St / Mission Rock St corner, fronting 3rd St -- 'marks the Mission Rock MUNI Metro Station along 3rd Street' per the D4D's own narrative text (Section 6.5.2). Part of the same larger Block D parcel as D2, subdivided into a residential tower (D1) and a parking structure (D2).

open_questions: The geometry file says the Design Controls describe D1 as marking the Mission Rock Muni Metro station; the Design Controls' Figure 2.3.1 shows the 'MUNI Metro stop' on Third Street but the quoted narrative sentence was not found in the April 2018 text.
Unit count and affordability for D1: none set; later phases may need more than 40% BMR to reach the project total after the 2025 Phase 1 cut.

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found in Port Commission agendas through February 2026; the block remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 surface parking lot (Lot A).
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block D1. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The DDA itself (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) places Parcel D1 in Phase 2 in its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) and its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of May 2023 for completing Phase 2's horizontal Phase Improvements -- already elapsed with Phase 2 not begun, and the Outside Date for actual completion is left to a future Phase Schedule that was never approved (Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones). No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 2 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date for this block.

2026-09-21 pass: the June 9, 2026 Port Commission item (Resolution 26-34, $10M pre-development investment) updates the earlier finding below that no Port memo gives a revised target year -- Port staff now have a schedule for Phase 2 pre-development work (through Fall 2027 contractor procurement) and a 'potential' construction start as early as Summer/Fall 2027, but the memo explicitly frames 2027/2028/2029 as alternative scenarios depending on when the Developer secures anchor tenants, not a single committed date -- still no basis (record, phase or project) for an expected-completion milestone for this block specifically.
